title: Generic ampleness of a supplied symmetric cubical line over a normal base
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $p:G\to S$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Here a commutative group scheme has addition, inverse and identity $e$ satisfying the commutative group identities, and separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion. Suppose every geometric fibre is semiabelian: over an algebraically closed residue-field extension $k$, it is an extension, exact as fppf sheaves, $1\to(\mathbf G_{m,k})^r\to G_k\to A_k\to1$, where $r\geq0$, $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$ with multiplication, and $A_k$ is a proper smooth geometrically connected $k$-group scheme. Write $\eta$ for the generic point of $S$ and suppose $G_\eta$ is proper over its residue field [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $(B,r_B,\tau_B)$ be a cubical rigidified line on $G$ [def-sfb-cubical-rigidified-line]. Suppose $B_\eta$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] and symmetric: $[-1]^*B_\eta\simeq B_\eta$, using tensor inverse image [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then $B$ is relatively ample over $S$: for every affine open $W\subseteq S$, $B|_{p^{-1}(W)}$ is ample. The line $B$ is supplied as input; this theorem asserts no existence of an extension from $G_\eta$ or from a dense open.

source.place: VI 3.0--3.1, normal connected-fibre cubical setting; Raynaud XI 1.13 (Lan cites XI 1.16). Originals WANTED. The stated locally Noetherian normal-base version is an agent prerequisite, cross-checked against Moret-Bailly VI 3.1 and Lan Lemma 4.2.1.6; Lan Chapter 4 by itself assumes a complete Noetherian adic base.

proof.text: For every nonempty affine open $T\subset S$, the hypotheses restrict to $T$, which is normal integral Noetherian and has the same generic point as $S$. Apply [lem-sfb-raynaud-generic-ample-power-model] to $H=G_T$ and $M=B_\eta$. This supplies an affine open covering of $T$ and, on each member, a relatively ample ordinary line $N$ and an integer $d\geq1$ with $N_\eta\simeq B_\eta^{\otimes d}$. The hypotheses used here are exactly the assumed semiabelian geometric fibres, smoothness, separatedness, finite presentation, proper generic fibre, and symmetry and ampleness of $B_\eta$. We shall compare $N$ with the supplied $B^{\otimes d}$, rather than asserting ampleness of $B$ from existence alone.

source.place: Agent assembly of the auxiliary existence input; original XI 1.13 / 1.16 WANTED

proof.text: Refine the affine covering so that $e^*N$ is free of rank one, and choose $r_N:e^*N\simeq\mathcal O_T$. This uses exactly Zariski local freeness of an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Relative ampleness of $N$ survives these restrictions by [lem-trf-scheme-relative-ample-base-change]. Write $C=B^{\otimes d}$ with the tensor-power rigidification. If $\alpha:N_\eta\simeq C_\eta$ is the supplied ordinary isomorphism, the two induced trivializations at $e_\eta$ differ by a scalar in $K^*$, $K=\kappa(\eta)$. Multiply $\alpha$ by its inverse scalar to make $\alpha$ rigidification-preserving. This changes neither the ordinary model nor its ampleness.

source.place: Tag 0893 (ample base change); rigidification normalization is an explicit scalar calculation

proof.text: The groups in the preceding restrictions have geometrically connected fibres, as required in [lem-sfb-semiabelian-cubical-rigidification](b). Explicitly, for a geometric fibre $E$ with torus kernel $Q$ and abelian quotient $A$, a clopen decomposition of $E$ gives a map $E\to\{0,1\}$. Its restriction to every geometric coset of $Q$ is constant because $Q$ is connected. It is therefore $Q$-invariant and descends along the fppf epimorphism $E\to A$ to a map $A\to\{0,1\}$, by the sheaf property. Since $A$ is connected this map is constant. Thus $E$ is connected. Case (b) of the cited cube theorem now equips $(N,r_N)$ with its unique compatible cubical structure. The supplied cube of $B$ gives one on $C=B^{\otimes d}$ by taking its $d$-fold tensor product: normalization, permutation invariance and the cocycle equation tensor to the corresponding equations. This is directly [def-sfb-cubical-rigidified-line].

source.place: I 2.6; explicit tensor-power construction and connectedness check, agent

proof.text: We spread the specified $\alpha$, not merely some isomorphism. On the current affine base $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ consider all finite subsets $F\subset A\setminus\{0\}$, ordered by inclusion, and $G_F=G\times_T\operatorname{Spec}A[(\prod F)^{-1}]$. This is a small nonempty directed index set. Each $G_F$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: $G\to T$ is of finite presentation and separated. Transitions are affine principal open immersions. Their limit is $G_\eta$: indeed compatible maps into the bases amount to a map to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ in which every nonzero element is invertible, hence uniquely to $\operatorname{Spec}K$; the compatible maps to $G_F$ also give their common map to $G$, and the fibre-product universal property finishes the assertion. The lines $N,C$ are finitely presented modules since they are locally free of rank one. Apply [lem-trf-fp-module-limit-isomorphism-descent] to these fixed models and $\alpha$. It yields inverse maps $u,v$ over some nonempty principal open $U\subset T$, with $u_\eta=\alpha$ and $v_\eta=\alpha^{-1}$. Thus $u:N|_{G_U}\simeq C|_{G_U}$, and $U$ is dense because $A$ is a domain.

source.place: Tag 01ZR, parts (2),(3), applied to fixed line models; explicit localization limit

proof.text: At the identity over $U$, the map $u$ is multiplication by a unit $a\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^*$ in the chosen rigidifications. Its generic value is $1$ since $u_\eta=\alpha$ is rigidified. The ring $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ is a localization of the domain $A$ and injects into $K$, so $a=1$. Hence $u$ preserves rigidifications. The final clauses of [lem-sfb-semiabelian-cubical-rigidification] say that cubes commute with restriction and that every rigidification-preserving isomorphism preserves them. They make $u$ a cubical rigidified isomorphism over the dense OPEN $U$.

source.place: I 2.6, functoriality and uniqueness; the scalar equality is elementary

proof.text: Apply only the full-faithfulness clause of [lem-sfb-normal-symmetric-cubical-extension] to the normal integral Noetherian base $T$, the dense open $U$, and the cubical rigidified lines $N,C$ on $G_T$. It extends $u$ to an isomorphism $N\simeq C$ on all of $G_T$. Its hypotheses hold on this restricted base: $G_T$ is smooth separated of finite presentation and all its geometric fibres are semiabelian. No assertion extending an isomorphism from the generic point alone is being used. Therefore $B^{\otimes d}=C$ is relatively ample over this $T$, by transport of the affine nonvanishing-locus definition of ampleness along $N\simeq C$.

source.place: II 3.2.1--3.2.3: full faithfulness over a dense open, not essential surjectivity

proof.text: For any affine open $V$ in this $T$, put $X=G_V$. Since $B^{\otimes d}|_X$ is ample, $X$ is quasi-compact and each $x\in X$ has a section $s$ of $(B^{\otimes d})^{\otimes m}$ for some $m\geq1$ with $x\in X_s$ and $X_s$ affine. Regard the same section as one of $B^{\otimes dm}$. Its stalk values and its nonvanishing locus are unchanged and $dm\geq1$. These are precisely the two conditions of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] for $B|_X$. Thus $B$ is relatively ample on each member of our affine covering. No separate tensor-power lemma is needed.

source.place: Tag 01PS, definition; elementary reflection of ampleness by a positive tensor power

proof.text: Doing this for an affine open covering of the original $S$ and the refinements above gives an affine open covering $S=\bigcup T_i$ on which $B|_{G_{T_i}}$ is ample. The original $p:G\to S$ is quasi-compact because it is of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Apply [lem-trf-scheme-relative-ample-affine-cover] with $h=p$ and $N=B$. It gives ampleness of $B|_{p^{-1}(W)}$ for EVERY affine open $W\subset S$, which is the required conclusion even when $S$ is not globally quasi-compact.

proof_origin.place: Assembly separating auxiliary ample existence, finite-presentation spreading, cubical full faithfulness and positive-power reflection. Raynaud and Moret-Bailly originals WANTED; Lan supplies corroboration only.
